summary: Graham County, AZ summit lookout on San Carlos Apache land; FFLA lists a two-story cab type at Standing*, whose asterisk means the structure stands with the cab no longer in place; other sources describe remnants or an abandoned building; build date not found; tribal permit needed.

facts.design: Tower (FFLA lists a two-story cab type; FFLA asterisk says the cab is no longer in place)
facts.status_note: FFLA lists Standing* for a two-story cab site; its key says the asterisk means the structure stands with the cab no longer in place. The Mountain Field Guide describes remnants at the summit; OpenStreetMap tags an abandoned building.

access.note: San Carlos Apache Tribe recreation permit required; remote approach, and an older lookout guide recommends four-wheel drive.

corrections.why: The cached OSM way tags abandoned:building=yes and tower:type=observation. Its page text does not say ruins.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLA lists Standing* with a two-story cab type, and its key says the asterisk means the structure stands with the cab no longer in place. So the cab is not standing, though FFLA says a structure remains. The Mountain Field Guide describes remnants and OpenStreetMap tags an abandoned building, so the current condition is uncertain.

notes_for_editor: No build date, builder or staffing years were found in any page read. HikeArizona search snippets give 1930 construction and a 1984 Dry Lake replacement, but HikeArizona returned HTTP 403 and was not used. The NHLR Dry Lake page describes a different, earlier 54-foot tower, not Willow. The FFLA asterisk key (read 2026-10-09) means the structure stands with the cab no longer in place; the earlier wording "marked as standing" ignored the asterisk and was corrected in the story. Access needs a San Carlos Apache Tribe permit; the story does not give a contact.
